b3-q84.analysis: Supported serverless Python execution reduces provisioning and manual lifecycle work for frequent small ad hoc tasks. Measure actual startup/idle behavior rather than assuming resources disappear instantly after every statement.
b3-q84.keyConcept: Supported serverless Python execution reduces provisioning and manual lifecycle work for frequent small ad hoc tasks. Measure actual startup/idle behavior rather than assuming resources disappear instantly after every statement.
b3-q84.examTip: Choose general Python-capable compute, not a SQL-only serving endpoint.

explanations.a: All-purpose compute supports ad hoc Python but requires more cluster lifecycle management and can remain idle. It is not the lowest-management fast-elastic option here.
explanations.b: Job clusters suit automated run lifecycles but introduce per-run provisioning and job orchestration for ad hoc work. They are not the direct managed interactive choice.
explanations.c: C supplies managed resource provisioning for supported Python workloads with less cluster administration. It best matches the short, frequent, low-management requirement.
explanations.d: A SQL warehouse is optimized for SQL execution, not arbitrary ad hoc Python scripts. It is the wrong execution interface for the stated language.

b3-q87.analysis: Commit, pull, merge, and clone can all be performed using Git tools outside Databricks Git folders. The question’s single Clone key is not uniquely supported by its wording.
b3-q87.keyConcept: Commit, pull, merge, and clone can all be performed using Git tools outside Databricks Git folders. The question’s single Clone key is not uniquely supported by its wording.
b3-q87.examTip: Outside Databricks describes where a Git client runs, not a limitation that leaves only clone possible.

explanations.a: Commit records local changes in a Git repository and is available in external Git clients. It is not exclusive to Databricks.
explanations.b: Pull obtains remote changes in an external working copy as well as in Git folders. It can be performed outside the platform.
explanations.c: Merge combines branches through external Git tooling too. Current Databricks also supports merging in its own Git workflow.
explanations.d: Clone creates a working copy and is certainly possible externally, but it is not the only listed external operation. Therefore the source D key cannot be uniquely graded.

b3-q88.analysis: Compute orchestration and the central Unity Catalog governance/metastore service are control-plane functions. Actual query/data processing, including serverless processing, runs in a compute plane rather than becoming control-plane work merely because Databricks manages it.
b3-q88.keyConcept: Compute orchestration and the central Unity Catalog governance/metastore service are control-plane functions. Actual query/data processing, including serverless processing, runs in a compute plane rather than becoming control-plane work merely because Databricks manages it.
b3-q88.examTip: Databricks-managed does not mean control plane: serverless execution still has its own compute plane.

explanations.a: Virtual machines executing workload code are compute resources. Their hosting account and lifecycle do not make the actual processing a control-plane function.
explanations.b: Compute orchestration schedules and manages resources from backend control services. It is a control-plane responsibility, distinct from executing the data tasks.
explanations.c: Serverless workloads execute in the serverless compute plane described by the architecture reference. Managed ownership does not convert their execution into the control plane.
explanations.d: Compute refers to processing the workload and belongs in the compute plane. It is not the administrative orchestration service.
explanations.e: Unity Catalog’s central governance/metastore service manages object metadata and permissions. Data storage and query enforcement/execution remain separate; this option does not mean every governed file resides in the control plane.
